entities.name: The Ottoman Archive Corpus
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The Ottoman Archive Corpus is one of the largest and most systematically organized bodies of administrative records from any pre-modern state, preserved primarily in the Başbakanlık Osmanlı Arşivi (Prime Ministry Ottoman Archives) in Istanbul. Spanning over six centuries (c. 1300–1922 CE), the archives contain an estimated 150 million documents including: kanunnames (sultanic law codes issued by Suleiman the Magnificent and successors), tahrir defterleri (cadastral tax surveys registering every household, farm, and village in the empire), mühimme defterleri (registers of important imperial orders), court records (şer'iyye sicilleri), vakıf (endowment) documents, diplomatic correspondence, and military records.

These archives provide an extraordinarily detailed portrait of Ottoman governance, economy, society, and daily life across a multi-ethnic, multi-religious empire spanning three continents.
